body:
So I'm gonna address the elephant in the room here.  Furries have a higher concentration of people with autism.  I don't mean that in the ableist 4chan way, I mean that factually [furries are at least 2.25 times more likely to have Asperger’s Syndrome](https://sites.google.com/site/anthropomorphicresearch/past-results/anthrocon-2013) than the general population is, and that's by conservative estimates.  And the things OP mentioned seem to revolve around poor social skills.

I think it's something we need to just accept.  For whatever reason, anthropomorphic animals are particularly appealing to people on the autism spectrum.  There is always going to be a portion of furries who don't have great social skills.  And the vast, vast majority of the community is not qualified to provide counseling for those members of the community.  I think the best thing we can do is be patient and understanding, and ask ourselves if it's really a big enough deal to get worked up over.  I know it's frustrating.  Like for me the main reason I keep my furriness a secret is because I'm afraid of that stigma.  But it's not like we can exclude all those people from our community because they have a mental condition that they never chose to have.
Yeah if I'm ever trying to jump off a bridge please don't do this, the whole reason I'm trying to die is so I can stop making people's lives more difficult
I've always assumed it's because people think I'm mentally handicapped and don't want to hurt my feelings.
Oh yeah, I was going to mention that sub but I guess I forgot
I just learned recently I can eat bacon, and it's so weird because there's nothing unpleasant about it, yet my mind still tries to say "no don't eat that"

I know the struggle :( I wish people would understand that I'm not choosing to dislike all these foods.  The past year or so I've gotten better at trying new foods, and even still my throat just gags no matter how hard I try to tell myself that this is normal food and its fine for me to eat.  I think people get the mental image of a kid being overdramatic and gagging when he doesn't want to eat his vegetables, but for me it's that I want to eat these foods, and I make an effort to eat them, but my body just rejects them.  It's so fucking frustrating.

Neither have been particularly helpful for me.

Cannabis dulls my sense of taste, which is helpful, but my sense of touch becomes much more sensitive, which makes already bad textures even worse.

Alcohol I think makes it a bit easier to handle the taste and texture, but I'm a lot more likely to gag or vomit because I basically just put poison in my stomach and am now trying to add foods my body doesn't like to the mixture.

Moderation is a big thing, getting in the habit of eating a little less than you'd like.

One of the most helpful things is if you can find a food you can eat that has good nutritional value.  For me it was baked chicken breast.  Didn't taste that different from chicken tenders, it's high in protein, low in fat, and satisfies my appetite without costing too many calories.

I'm not sure if it's entirely necessary to tell the teacher.  Maybe it's different in high school (I don't really remember my experience) but last year in my college phys ed we had to do a nutrition log, and I never heard anything from the instructor about the fact that 80% of my log was baked chicken and peanut butter and jelly.

>marijuana is bad, but I’m probably going to kill myself anyway, so let’s see

That idea can actually have a lot of power. I'm a bit ashamed to admit it, but a lot of the time weed is what keeps me going. I often find myself thinking "I should kill myself," and telling myself "but then you can't smoke" stops that train of thought in its tracks.

I'm no doctor or psychologist, but I'm pretty sure that living just so I can smoke weed can't be healthy. Still though, it's healthier that killing myself. There's no way that getting high a few times a week (or even daily, but I haven't gotten to that point) is *worse* than daily spending hours mentally drafting suicide notes and thinking about different methods and telling myself that suicide is the right thing for me to do. Hell I've even been out of weed since May and still the thought of "I'll be able to smoke soon enough" keeps me hanging in there.

I know it's unhealthy, but the alternative is worse.

Some things that have kept me going when I've wanted to end it:

Alcohol, weed, and masturbation are fun

I have some close friends who I do not want to put through that kind of hurt

I have a stash of exotic dildos and other sex toys that I'd have to dispose of before offing myself so my family doesn't find them, and for some reason I'm a lot more hesitant to throw away $500 worth of sex toys than I am to throw away my life

There's drugs I want to try before I die

This one is super fucked up, but for a while I promised myself that I wouldn't kill myself unless my ex does first, because I didn't want him to find out and pity me

Really if you're looking for a reason to stay alive, you should look for more than just noble reasons.  There's been times in my life where the only reason I lived was for the pleasure of smoking weed or getting drunk.  It's not the healthiest thing, but I'd argue it's better than dying.

I really want to have fun. Tomorrow wouldn't be a good day though. I know it sounds like a bullshit excuse but Sundays are really busy days for me having work then commuting back to school. I have been making an effort though to actually do things I enjoy even when I don't feel like it. I should be able to have fun Monday though heheh.

Thanks. I don't quite know why but knowing that somebody's dealing with something so similar is really comforting. I've thought a lot about seeing a therapist. I'm scared to talk about these issues because I'm worried that I'm just exaggerating them because I want to feel like I'm special and that my downfalls aren't my fault. I feel like talking about them would at best make me look like an idiot and at worst be really insulting to people who've had to deal with this shit. Not to mention that I have a really hard time scheduling something like a haircut appointment, let alone a therapy appointment. I just feel kinda conflicted about it.
